summary: 52-year-old woman with spontaneous blood-stained discharge from a single duct of the left nipple for 5 weeks, no palpable lump. NICE NG12: ≥50 with unilateral nipple discharge → suspected cancer pathway; mammography + ultrasound; duct excision (microdochectomy) for diagnosis.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Blood-stained discharge from the left nipple
inputs.hpi: Five weeks of spontaneous blood-stained discharge from the left nipple, staining her bra. Comes from one spot on the nipple. No lump noticed, no pain. Postmenopausal. Not on any medicines.

exam.other: Breasts: no palpable mass. Left nipple: spontaneous and expressible blood-stained discharge from a single duct at 3 o'clock; trigger point at the areolar margin. No skin change, no axillary nodes.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Spontaneous bloody single-duct nipple discharge (left) — ?intraductal papilloma, exclude DCIS/carcinoma
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Spontaneous blood-stained single-duct nipple discharge (left), age 52, no mass. Suspected cancer pathway. Bilateral mammography and retroareolar ultrasound; microdochectomy for histology if imaging normal.

mustNotMiss.note: Bloody single-duct discharge: papilloma is commonest but DCIS/carcinoma must be excluded.

redFlags.note: NICE NG12: aged 50 and over with, in one breast only, nipple discharge, retraction or other changes of concern.

mustExclude.note: Reassurance without imaging is inappropriate for spontaneous bloody single-duct discharge.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web, since the engine-matching fixes (2026-09): the Assessment management panel now follows the confirmed diagnosis (paneDiseaseId duct_ectasia) instead of the PANE leader; the duct ectasia protocol offers "reassurance; evening primrose oil". There is no nipple-discharge / single-duct bloody discharge protocol.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral
guideline.section: Site-specific recommendations: breast cancer (age ≥30 unexplained lump; ≥50 unilateral nipple discharge/retraction; skin changes; men ≥50 subareolar mass), haematological cancers (unexplained lymphadenopathy), head and neck (unexplained thyroid lump)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral. NICE guideline NG12. London: NICE; 2015 (updated).

guideline.name: NCCN Guidelines — Breast Cancer Screening and Diagnosis
guideline.section: Palpable mass: age <30 ultrasound first; age ≥30 diagnostic mammography + ultrasound; tissue sampling of suspicious findings; nipple discharge (spontaneous, unilateral, single duct, bloody); skin changes
guideline.citation: National Comprehensive Cancer Network. NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Breast Cancer Screening and Diagnosis (current version at authoring).

guideline.name: Best practice diagnostic guidelines for patients presenting with breast symptoms (ABS / RCR, Department of Health)
guideline.section: Triple assessment (clinical examination, age-appropriate imaging, needle biopsy); imaging by age; nipple discharge; breast infection; breast pain
guideline.citation: Willett AM, Michell MJ, Lee MJR (eds). Best practice diagnostic guidelines for patients presenting with breast symptoms. London: Department of Health / Association of Breast Surgery; 2010.

rationale: Base nipple-discharge case with the high-risk pattern (spontaneous, unilateral, single duct, bloody, age ≥50). The ICD N64.52 (nipple discharge) is how this is coded before histology.
